subject: Gaia Health: unexpected throughput degradation impacting dedicated pool
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta@gaiahealth.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@gaiahealth.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T08:52:00-07:00
Subject: Increased errors & timeouts on our dedicated pool (prod)

Hi Markus,

Over the last ~40 minutes we've been seeing a steady spike in inference timeouts (500 errors and client-side retry loops) from our production dedicated pool. This started right after a normal traffic surge. Throughput dropped ~45% for our baseline model and several of our pipelines are queueing. Our ops team pulled logs and attached a short excerpt (see capacity_log_excerpt.txt) showing repeated "KV cache miss" warnings and a flurry of allocation timeouts to the dedicated nodes.

Can you confirm whether there's an ongoing issue on Redwood's side (autoscale / reserved pool)? This is impacting patient-facing suggestions — we need an ETA and mitigation ASAP.

Marta
Sr. Platform Engineer, Gaia Health
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T08:58:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased errors & timeouts on our dedicated pool (prod)

Thanks for flagging, Marta — I see the same alerts on Redwood's SLO board.

Internal: Monica / SRE, can you triage immediately? Priorities: 1) determine whether autoscaler failed to hydrate warm nodes, 2) confirm whether fallback routing to our GPU burst tier occurred, 3) identify any recent infra changes to eviction thresholds.

Laura — I'll draft a short customer update to send in 30 minutes; please prepare credit/contract talking points if we need to offer a short-term credit. Karthik — please standby for account-level outreach if we need an SLA exception.

I'll loop back with status in 15.

-Markus
VP, Customer Reliability
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased errors & timeouts on our dedicated pool (prod) — initial findings

Markus / team,

Quick triage notes (attached excerpt):
- Observation: Autoscaler attempted to add warm nodes but the warm pool controller failed to complete preflight due to a race when invalidating local KV caches. This led to repeated allocation timeouts and left requests queued.
- Root cause (prelim): A recent change in the warm-pool eviction window (deployed 03/09) tightened the window; combined with a concurrent cache-invalidation job, some nodes reported stale cache metadata and were rejected by the runtime safety checks.
- Impact: ~40-55% throughput degradation for Gaia's pool for ~36 minutes before manual intervention.

Immediate mitigations we applied (09:18):
1) Manually forced warm-pool resume for Gaia's reservation (command: redwoodctl warmpool resume --customer gaia --count 8).
2) Bumped target replica count for the pool to +25% while we stabilize.
3) Enabled temporary fallback routing to the burst tier for latency-sensitive routes (config change id Ops-9823).

Next steps:
- Roll back the eviction-window tightening in canary within 2 hours.
- Ship a patch to the warm-pool controller to remove the invalidation race (estimate 24–36h for full deploy and validation).
- Draft a formal postmortem and propose a credit for impacted time.

I've attached capacity_log_excerpt.txt for the customer(s). If you want, I can prepare an engineer-facing timeline for the follow-up postmortem.

-Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-03-11T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased errors & timeouts on our dedicated pool (prod) — customer comms draft

Markus / Monica,

I put together a concise customer note below — let me know edits and I can send from your mailbox once approved. Also prepared a short note on credits and next steps for legal/finance.

--- DRAFT CUSTOMER UPDATE ---
Subject: Incident update: reduced throughput for Gaia Health dedicated pool (Mar 11)
Hi Marta —
We’re sorry for the disruption earlier today. Summary: between 08:20–08:56 PT we observed degraded throughput for your dedicated GPU pool resulting from an interaction between a recently adjusted warm-pool eviction window and our cache invalidation process. This caused nodes to fail safety checks during autoscale and delayed scaling events.
What we did: manually resumed your warm pool, temporarily increased replica targets, and routed latency-sensitive requests to our burst tier. We’ve rolled the canary rollback to revert the eviction change and are preparing a patch to eliminate the cache-invalidation race.
Next steps: a full patch rollout and validation within 24–36 hours, followed by a formal postmortem that will include corrective actions and a proposed credit for the impacted window.
ETA for formal postmortem: March 12 (written report + timeline).
We’ll keep you updated and are standing by to discuss on a call if useful.
Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
--- end draft ---

Laura
Director, Customer Success
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: ops@gaiahealth.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update: reduced throughput for Gaia Health dedicated pool (Mar 11)

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the quick alert and the log excerpt. Short update:
- Incident window: ~08:20–08:56 PT today; impact was reduced throughput and intermittent 500s for some pipelines.
- What happened: a recent change to our warm-pool eviction window interacted with a cache-invalidation job, causing a race that prevented some warm nodes from passing preflight checks during autoscale.
- Immediate actions taken: we manually resumed your warm pool, increased replica targets, and routed latency-sensitive traffic to our burst tier (this restored acceptable throughput within ~12 minutes of intervention).
- Next steps: we rolled the canary to revert the eviction-window change and are preparing a code patch to remove the invalidation race. We expect full patch rollout + verification in 24–36 hours.
- Postmortem & credits: we will publish a written postmortem by March 12 with root cause, fixes, and a proposed service credit for the impacted period.

I’ve attached the log excerpt you sent for transparency. Please share any additional telemetry that will help with our RCA. Happy to jump on a call — LMK a time that works.

-Markus
VP, Customer Reliability
